description: Release wires and ACH batches for the office, the 10 family entities, and family members (about 15 wires a month: capital calls, tax payments, large purchases); act as second approver on subsidiary payments over $25,000 (about 30 a month)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A missed capital call or tax payment can cost a default penalty or interest; subsidiaries cannot pay large suppliers or payroll taxes without the office's second approval; one fraudulent wire would exceed $50,000. RPO 4 h because approved instructions live in email between bank sessions
manual_workaround: Banks and custodians accept phoned instructions only with callback to numbers on file; the Principal is backup approver on every bank portal; subsidiaries can ask the bank for a one-day approval change by signed letter
dependent_third_parties: Two banks and two custodians (portals and tokens); productivity suite vendor; internet provider; MSP
dependent_people_or_facilities: Controller; Family Office Director; Principal (backup approver); bank hardware tokens

business_process: Family bill pay and household payroll
description: Pay about 140 family bills a month from family members' own accounts; run biweekly payroll for 5 household employees and the 7 office employees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Household employees must be paid on the biweekly date; late payroll tax deposits bring penalties; utility, insurance, and tuition bills carry late fees and coverage lapses after a few days
manual_workaround: Pay urgent bills directly in the family members' bank portals; repeat the prior payroll through the payroll service's phone line; keep a printed list of due dates for the next 14 days
dependent_third_parties: Bill pay vendor; payroll service; banks

description: Investment decisions, trade and rebalancing instructions to the two custodians, capital call funding, and private deal documents for family clients
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Capital call notices give about 10 business days, but a late call can trigger default terms in a private fund; markets can move against an unexecuted rebalancing; custodians keep the official record, so data loss is limited to the office's working files
manual_workaround: Phone instructions to the custodians with their own callback and verification; position data from custodian websites instead of SYS-06; defer non-urgent rebalancing
dependent_third_parties: Two custodians; investment platform vendor; productivity suite vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Investment Director; Investment Analyst; Family Office Director (backup)

description: Monthly review of each subsidiary's financial package; board meetings; consolidation in SYS-01; quarterly covenant reporting to the subsidiaries' bank lender
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly packages are due on business day 10; the lender's quarterly covenant certificate is due 45 days after quarter end, so a few days' delay is absorbed except in the last week before a lender deadline
manual_workaround: Subsidiary controllers email packages to a backup address or deliver them on encrypted USB; consolidation done in a spreadsheet from the subsidiaries' trial balances
dependent_third_parties: Accounting system vendor; subsidiaries' own systems and IT providers; productivity suite vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Controller; Subsidiary Presidents and their controllers

business_process: Family entity accounting and tax coordination
description: Books for the office and the 10 family entities; capital accounts and K-1 allocations for CSC Family Investments, LLC on SYS-11; tax document exchange with the outside CPA firm; quarterly estimated tax payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Normally a week of slack; in the two weeks before a tax or K-1 deadline the tolerance drops to about 2 days, because late K-1s delay the family's returns and late estimated payments bring penalties
manual_workaround: Prepare estimates from the prior quarter; ask the CPA firm for an extension; rebuild K-1 allocations from the prior year file and custodian statements
dependent_third_parties: Accounting system vendor; cloud provider and MSP (SYS-11); outside CPA firm; vault vendor

business_process: Family records and emergency document access
description: Keep and retrieve estate plans, health care directives, insurance policies, passports, and driver licenses for family members; respond to urgent requests (a hospital asking for a directive, a lost passport while traveling)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A health care directive or insurance policy may be needed within hours in an emergency; documents change rarely, so a day of data loss is tolerable
manual_workaround: Originals of estate plans and directives are held by outside counsel; family members keep copies of their own directives at home; insurers and counsel can resend policies

description: Quarterly performance and position reports for each family member and entity; ad hoc net worth statements for lenders and insurers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reports are quarterly and are not time-critical within a two-week window; custodian data can be pulled again from the source
manual_workaround: Pull statements from custodian websites and prepare a summary spreadsheet

description: Email, calendars, and chat for staff, family members, subsidiaries, and vendors; board meetings; office administration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Email is the channel for nearly every request and approval; the Principal's and family members' calendars and travel plans live there, and staff cannot reach family members or subsidiaries without it for more than a day
manual_workaround: Phones and text messages using the printed contact card; temporary mailbox in the vendor's web portal from a clean device; board materials printed
dependent_third_parties: Productivity suite vendor; MSP; internet provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Office Manager; all staff; office suite
